vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-4176
vulnerability.description: Perl heap overflow; fixed upstream in 5.43.9 / 5.42.2-rc1 / 5.40.4-rc1

statements.impact_statement: nixpkgs applies the upstream fix as a source patch without a version bump: pkgs/development/interpreters/perl/interpreter.nix references CVE-2026-4176 on nixos-26.05 and nixos-unstable (backported via NixOS/nixpkgs PR #528021). The perl 5.42.0 shipped in these images is built from that patched expression, so the version-only match is a false positive. NOT valid for images built from nixos-25.05/25.11, which never received the backport — this statement was added together with the base ref bump to nixos-26.05.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-13221
vulnerability.description: Perl regexp memory corruption with large tries (Perl/perl5 GH #23388); nixpkgs ships 5.42.0 without the guard on every channel

statements.impact_statement: Scoped to the tracelabs profile ONLY; deliberately not catalog-wide. Reaching the defect requires BOTH (1) a regex whose fixed-string alternation exceeds U16_MAX regnodes and (2) regex debugging enabled. Condition 2 was verified to be genuinely required against stock perl 5.42.0: the upstream reproducer (Perl/perl5 GH #23388) dies rc=255 "regexp memory corruption" with `use re "Debug"`, and runs clean without the pragma at reproducer size, at 4x that size, and with a single huge alternation. IMPORTANT: the pragma is NOT a security boundary — PERL5OPT=-Mre=Debug reproduces the crash without editing any script (verified). The load-bearing leg is therefore condition 1, the absence of a qualifying alternation. Runtime perl consumers in this image were enumerated with `nix why-depends --precise` over the profile's own packages, its five `requires` profiles and the resolute base: kasmvnc (bin/.kasmvncserver-wrapped, a Perl script), xdg-utils (bin/xdg-screensaver runs `perl -e`, reached via the chromium/firefox/brave wrappers) and exiftool. Nothing else in this image reaches perl at runtime. Each was compiled under -Mre=Debug on STOCK perl with the real PERL5LIB, alongside a control canary that DOES crash under the same harness: kasmvncserver and all 16 bundled KasmVNC modules, and the xdg-screensaver one-liner, all compile with zero corruption. Neither builds an alternation dynamically (no `join "|"` anywhere); kasmvncserver's 27 regex operations are small literals interpolating single scalars. exiftool's interpreter is separately REMEDIATED, not merely unreachable: the overlay applies the upstream fix (commit 03f74bbb) to the perl exiftool compiles against, so the shipped derivation carries CVE-2026-13221.patch and passes the reproducer rc=0 where stock dies. RESIDUAL, stated rather than omitted: `perl -c` compiles literal regexes and `use`d modules but NOT regexes assembled at runtime from data. The interpolated scalars above ($host, $window_id, $defaultVisualId) could in principle carry `|` characters, but an attacker would need to control them AND set the pragma, both of which require already holding the privileges of the process being attacked (same-user; terminal access is already granted in this image). No privilege boundary is crossed. NOT VALID for other profiles. inkscape reaches perl through enchant -> hspell -> bin/multispell, a consumer whose regexes have NOT been examined; perl 5.42.0 is the same store path in both, so only the profile scope separates them. Verified at nixpkgs rev 5b4f72e1705a63aace42900610c4db82cb4af0ec on 2026-08-03. Upstream GH #23388 is still OPEN (the fix declines to build an overflowing trie rather than repairing the 16-bit field). CVE severity and the first upstream release carrying the guard were NOT verified here and must be checked against NVD / perl5 release notes before use in any customer-facing risk statement.
